utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We'll hear the testimony of four witnesses through videolink today. Until now, we have received no applications for protective measures. Would that still be the situation?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I was informed that we'll start with Mr. Babacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then could we first establish whether the videolink is properly functioning. I can see the representative of the registry in, I take it, Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Good morning, Your Honours, this is the registrar representative in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In Zagreb, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] And we hear you fine and see you fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the same is true in the opposite direction.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I think the proper procedure would be that since the witnesses move from 92 bis to 92 ter that we first get the attestations, Mr. Misetic. Are you ready to call the first witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I am, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Madam Registrar, in Zagreb, would you be so kind to escort or have Mr. Babacic being escorted into the courtroom or at least in your room, and could you confirm that apart from the technician and yourself there is no one present in that room.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] I confirm that, Your Honour. It's only myself and the technician.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you, please, see that Mr. Babacic enters the courtroom. Good morning, Mr. Babacic. Can you see me and can you hear me in a language you understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you also can hear me, I take it, from your answer in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Babacic, before you give evidence the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require that you make a -- that you give a solemn declaration, that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text of that solemn declaration is now handed out to you by the representative of the registry. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Babacic. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Babacic, you will first be briefly examined by Mr. Misetic. Mr. Misetic is counsel for Mr. Gotovina. Mr. Misetic, please, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Babacic. Would you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Good morning. Josko Babacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And, Madam Registrar, if we could show the witness Exhibit D200, please. And if we could have that on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Babacic, do you recall giving a statement to the Gotovina Defence and signing that statement on the 8th of May, 2008?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And is that your signature in the bottom right-hand corner of that statement that's in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Have you had a chance to review this statement?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Are there any changes or additions that need to be made to the statement?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: No, there's no need.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: At the time you gave the statement, did you give it to the best of your knowledge and in accordance with the truth?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If I asked you the same questions today in court, would provide the same answers today in court that you provided to investigators of the Gotovina Defence on the 8th of May, 2008?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I move to admit Exhibit D200 into evidence. MS. DE LANDRI: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Microphone, could you please activate your microphone. MS. DE LANDRI: Yes. No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. De Landri. A number had already been assigned, Mr. Registrar. Therefore, D200 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. That concludes my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Babacic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Misetic. Ms. De Landri, are you ready to cross-examine the witness? MS. DE LANDRI: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Babacic, you will now be cross-examined by Ms. De Landri. Ms. De Landri is counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Ms. De Landri. MS. DE LANDRI: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Mr. Babacic, you gave your statement on May 8th of 2008; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And your statement pertains to events that occurred in August and September of 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Just the month of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And I'd like to direct your attention to paragraph 2 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity to look at paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: You were the assistant commander of the Political Activity Department of the 2nd Battalion of the 113th Brigade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Can you describe what your duties as the assistant commander of the Political Activity Department were?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: My duties were to prepare soldiers, to talk to them, sometimes disciplinary measures. In any case, maintaining the state of morale.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And also directing your attention to paragraph 2, you stated: "The 2nd Infantry Battalion was comprised of conscripts." Can you name some of those conscripts?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: I no longer remember. I know Filipovic, Grbic. There were hundreds of soldiers throughout all that time, the conscripts changed, so I can't be sure of their names. We're talking hundreds of soldiers who went through the unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And directing your attention to paragraph 5 of your statement. In paragraph 5, you stated that the brigade commander ordered that, "... preparations, for the treatment of civilians and POWs be given." Can you tell us who the brigade commander was who gave that order?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Danijel Kotlar was the commander. But this was not preparation for the treatment of prisoners of war but, rather, instructions to the soldiers as to how behave in combat, how to treat civilians, the wounded, and they were distributed booklets where they could find all that. First of all, the soldiers provide -- were given explanations. The booklet was read out to them and then they were distributed, the booklets which contained instructions issued by the Red Cross. Each and every one of them was given this booklet which contained the instructions by the Red Cross and the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Just so I'm clear on your answer, you do not recall who the brigade commander was who gave those instructions that I asked about?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't say that. I remember that Danijel Kotlar was the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was -- that was the beginning of the previous answer. MS. DE LANDRI: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the preparations were conducted?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: The preparations were conducted in a village called Velim in Stampoti, and we followed those items, and on that day, we launched the operation, all of the soldiers in my unit were comprised with the preparations and instructions.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And directing your attention to paragraph 6 of your statement, you said that all soldiers received a booklet on conduct in accordance with the Geneva Conventions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Did you personally observe soldiers receiving those booklets?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: I distributed the booklets myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And was that on August 4th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: On the 3rd of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Who prepared the booklets?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: They arrived from the brigade command. I don't know who had prepared them. I received them from the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to direct your attention now to paragraph 9 of your statement. Do you have paragraph 9 in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Okay. In paragraph 9 you stated: "We had a meeting with members of the reconnaissance company in the village of Bribirske." How many men attended that meeting; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: That was not a meeting. This is when the units linked up. My unit linked up with the reconnaissance company that had arrived from a different directions. This was the point where our two units linked up. It was not a meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: So -- so I -- just to clarify your answer. There -- there was not a meeting?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did meet, but it was my unit linking up with another unit. My unit had over 200 men and the reconnaissance company had about 30 men. There were tanks there, and there were some 30 men who had arrived as members of the reconnaissance company. They had arrived from a different direction, and that's where our two units met.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Can you name any of the individuals who attended that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I object to the form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're referring to a meeting where the witness just testified there was no meeting, Ms. De Landri. So perhaps you asked the witness whether he knew anyone of the units that met at that point in time. MS. DE LANDRI: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you understood the question, Mr. Babacic? The question being whether you could name any of the members of the units that met at that moment in time at that place.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I was the commander of that reconnaissance company two months before that, and I knew all the men from that company. And I also knew all the men from my unit and all of my commanders were with me, and I can give you all of their names, if you want me to do so. MS. DE LANDRI:

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Let me say -- do you want me to give you the names of the men from my unit or from the reconnaissance company? Which names do you want me to give you?

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Tell us the names as best you can recall from the men who were there at the gathering, not meeting, as I incorrectly stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The witness asked whether he should give the names only of his unit or of the reconnaissance unit, which met with his units at the time, the reconnaissance unit which he had had command over before. Both units or ... MS. DE LANDRI: Both, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ivica Mikulandra, the battalion commander then Miljanic Robano [phoen], Ruzic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. For the transcribers to follow, could you give them one by one and slowly. So could you first focus on your own unit and then give us the first name that comes to your mind.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The battalion commander Ivica Mikulandra from my unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Carefully look at Ms. De Landri because she'll give you a sign when she expects you to -- the next name to be mentioned. Next one, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Miljanic, the company commander. Banovac, the company commander. Ruzic, the company commander. Strunje, a platoon commander. Colak, a platoon commander. Zura, a platoon commander. These are the names of some of the commanders of companies in my battalion and there was also me at the forefront. And the person I met first was Krsto Friganovic from the reconnaissance company. There was also Zeljko Kulusic in that unit. Dubravko Ivetic was another man from that company. Vrlika. What do I know? I really can't remember any more names, but I can recall their faces very well and I knew all the men that were there. Vuksic was the commander of the reconnaissance company, I just remembered. MS. DE LANDRI:

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: I'm directing your attention to paragraph 11 of your statement, on August 14th, it says: "We conducted heavy offensive activities in the areas of Trubar and Babici and we seized the said villages the same evening." Can you recall anyone who was there at the time, any of the other men who were there during that occurrence?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: The same members of the units that I just mentioned. And I'm talking only about my unit, because the reconnaissance unit was not with us in that territory.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Directing your attention to paragraph 12 of your statement. You stated on August 15th of 1995 you were wounded, is that correct, and taken to a medical centre?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: What type of wound did you suffer?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: I suffered a wound in the left hand, from hand-grenade shrapnel and a fracture of my left leg.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the medical centre?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: I was just -- I received first aid at the medical centre, and then I was discharged and stayed at home for a few months.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Did you stay in the hospital overnight?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: You mean the night between the 15th and the 16th?

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Any night.

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: But when -- when was the time that you went home for a few months because of your wounds?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: I was wounded around 11.00, and around 1300 hours I was put into a car. The journey to Sibenik took about two or three hours. In the afternoon on the 15th, I arrived at the hospital where I was examined by the doctors. I don't know how long the whole examination lasted, but it was sometime in the evening when I was taken home. Around midnight, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And after that time, you stayed at home for several months?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes. My leg was in a plaster. I could not move, and I had to take the rehabilitation exercises.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Directing your attention to paragraph 9 of your statement. In paragraph 9 you stated that -- oh, I'm sorry. Paragraph 9, that's correct. You stated you did not encounter Vladimir Gojanovic on August 5th, 1995. Can you describe how you know Vladimir Gojanovic?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes. I know him personally because his mother and mine worked for the same company. I know him as a child. I know his brother who had been a very good friend of mine and comrade-in-arms ever since the start of the war. I know his other brother. His wife was my class-mate in the primary school. It's a small town; I simply know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: So when would have been the last time you saw him from August of 1995?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Do you mean --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the latter part of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat? MS. DE LANDRI: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: When was the last you would have seen him from -- that you can recall from August of 1995, prior to August of 1995?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't recall him at all, seeing him at that time. No, I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: When you were the political activity director of the unit, how many men did you have under your command?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: I was not a commander; I was an assistant commander. My duty was not that of a commander but simply to prepare the men in my field. However, I had received the task to prepare the men for combat. In other words, I did not have a commanding duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: I just want to make sure that the question was clear. Your statement in paragraph 2 says you were the assistant commander of the Political Activity Department of the 2nd Battalion of the HV 113th Brigade. My question is: In that capacity, how many men did you have working for you?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: There were three of us, I believe. We worked together.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And would that be three men in addition to yourself?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: There was I and two others.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And who were the two other individuals?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Zdenko Knezovic and Andjelko Zepna.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Zepina, interpreter's correction. MS. DE LANDRI:

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And what were their responsibilities?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Same as mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that you all shared the same rank?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: I think we did, in fact. I'm not sure, but I believe that we had the same rank.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention to paragraph 13 of your statement. In paragraph 13 you say: "As assistant commander of the Political Activity Department, and as former commander of the reconnaissance company, and having commanded units during the operation, I often communicated with other commanders, led takeovers of units in positions, and I can say with certainty that I did not see Vladimir Gojanovic as a member of any unit." Can you tell us who the other commanders you communicated with, that you referred to in paragraph 13?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: With the commander of the reconnaissance company, the commander of the 3rd Battalion, assistant for political activity of the 3rd Battalion, commanders of the 1st Battalion. In other words, with all the commanders who held positions, who were at positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Can you tell us their names?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Commander of the 3rd Battalion, Dragan Rak. Assistant for political activity, Boris Slavica -- the late Boris Slavica, he was killed. The commander of the 1st Battalion was Emil Males. The command of the reconnaissance company, Ivica Vuksic. Commander of the tank battalion, Gojanovic -- I don't remember --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Bojanovic, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bojanovic. I don't recall his first name. Commanders of companies: Drezgan, Djaja, Prolic. One of them was called Bajulji commander of the tank platoon, Sudac. There were other men whose names I can't recall now, but I'm certain I would recognise them if I saw them. MS. DE LANDRI:

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: You mentioned an individual the -- Dragan Rak; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Have you been in contact with him since 1995?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: As I said, Sibenik is a small town. We do come across each other every now and then, have a drink together and have a talk, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity to discuss your testimony with him here today?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: We came here together, but we did not touch upon these topics, since we were not on our own. We were not, the two of us, alone.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Since you gave your written statement in May of 1998 [sic] were you also aware that he gave a written statement in connection with this case?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe counsel means May of 2008. MS. DE LANDRI: Yes, I apologise, you're correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: May of 2008.

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And did you discuss your statements at any time, between May of 2008 and today?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: We discussed our participation in Operation Storm in general terms, but I'm not aware of the contents of his statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: You also mentioned a -- if I'm pronouncing the name correctly, a Mr. Sudac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Okay. And you're aware that he gave a statement in connection with this case; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And have you seen him locally since August and September of 1995?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: I didn't see that much of him because he is very busy and he does not reside in Sibenik. He resides in Vodice, so I hardly ever see him.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: You testified earlier that the soldiers that were -- that you instructed were given booklets in accordance with the -- or to instruct them on the treatment of civilians, and that's also in your statement. In your personal observation, did the soldiers who you came into contact with act in accordance with those instructions?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Okay. MS. DE LANDRI: I'd like the witness to be shown Defence Exhibit 205.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: In particular, I'd like to direct your attention to paragraph number 2, and the date on the document, which is August 12th.

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Okay. And the document is an order signed by the commander, I believe you mentioned previously, Danijel Kotlar. And paragraph 2 specifically says that: "... all necessary measures are to be taken by the troops to participate very actively in exhibiting military and disciplinary behaviour and maintaining order in the zone of responsibility, preventing arson, looting of property and all other illegal acts. Take stringent disciplinary measures against perpetrators of such acts." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Do you know why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no. The witness may answer the question. MS. DE LANDRI: I'm not sure --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe the question wasn't completed yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Babacic, the portion that was read and the portion that you see on -- in this order, the question was why this was written in this order.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You should put that question to the person who drafted the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you know, please, tell us; if you don't know, tell us as well, but don't --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. MS. DE LANDRI: One more question, one follow-up question along that line, if I may, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Do you know why -- you were under the command of Commander Kotlar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Do you know why he would have written such an order, if he had not observed these acts being participated in?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Well, he probably wrote it down because he wanted to. I didn't see any of those things happening. The date is the 12th of August. Between the 10th and 14th of August I was on the state border beyond Srb. I was holding positions there and had no contact with the remainder of the units. MS. DE LANDRI: Your Honour, I don't have any further questions, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. De Landri. Mr. Misetic, first of all, I had forgotten to ask but I think there were no -- was no need for cross-examination by the other Defence teams. Mr. Misetic, any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I just had one question because I wasn't sure if the witness understood the question. So it's related to the question and answer at page 12, lines 19 to 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Babacic, if I could just ask you, do you recall seeing Vladimir Gojanovic at any time prior to the 1st of August, 1995? Did you ever see him before the 1st of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I certainly did. But it may have been in 1993 or 1994. But I did not see him wearing a uniform of the Croatian Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Babacic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Babacic, I may have a few questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Babacic, could you tell us how you were approached for the purpose of giving a statement, the statement you gave on the 8th of May, 2008.

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: I think that a man came, by the name of Jozo, as early as 2006. We had a meeting with a lawyer from the Defence team; I don't recall his name. I only know that he passed away. And then in 2008, the man came and asked me about my participation in the action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said a meeting in 2006. A meeting, was that just you and the person you just described, or were there other persons as well?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: No, no. There were several commanders there, but I recall only that one lawyer. I don't know if he was from the ICTY or, rather, from the OTP, or from the Defence. I don't even know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then you said there were several commanders. Could you tell us approximately -- could you give us some names and could you give us the number of persons present during this meeting in 2006.

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: No, it was a brief meeting. There were several commanders, and I don't recall all the names at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What did you discuss during this brief meeting?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Only our participation in Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was it mentioned at that time that Mr. Gojanovic may have given statements or that he might be a potential witness before the --

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: No. We -- no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the name of Mr. Gojanovic was not mentioned at all during that meeting?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: No. It certainly was not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now before you gave your statement in 2008, did you receive a phone call; did someone come to your place? What happened before you gave that statement.

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: The individual came whom I gave my statement to. His name is written there. He's called Jozo. I gave him the statement and that was it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He came to your house?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes. He phoned me, and then we met up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You met in your house and that's where you gave your statement; or did you give your statement somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: No. I gave my statement on the premises of the HVIDRA, which is the association of war veterans in Sibenik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Have you seen any other person -- yes, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think there's a -- if he could explain what HVIDRA is again, because I'm not certain that the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I'll invite the witness to do that. Could you again explain what the HVIDRA is or -- I may pronounce it wrongly, but the organisation on which premises --

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: It's HVIDRA, the H-v-i-d-r-a is the association of the Croatian war veterans, veterans of the homeland war. Or rather, the -- of the war invalids of the homeland war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you gave your statement, did you see any other person who may have been there for the purpose of giving a statement as well?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: The office consisted of several rooms and I was giving my statement in a room where I was alone with Jozo. There were several individuals. There were more people in the other rooms on the premises of the HVIDRA office and in front of the office itself. But I was giving the statement on my own to the individual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you speak to the other individuals before you gave the statement?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes. But we didn't know what it was all about. We engaged in guess-work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what did you guess?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: We were guessing that it was about Operation Storm but we didn't know exactly what.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was the name Gojanovic mentioned at that point by anyone, either Jozo who interviewed you, or any of the other persons present?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Only Jozo spoke to me. He asked me if I had ever seen Gojanovic before. I told him that I knew him personally, but I didn't see him -- but I didn't see him there at that time. I think this is contained in my statement. I would not have said it had he not asked me about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I'm interested in to know is whether the name of Mr. Gojanovic was mentioned at any point in time prior to the interview taken by Jozo.

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't know anything about it, until I had that conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On your statement, we find --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, that interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On your statement, we find that you're retired. Are you a -- do you have no professional occupation at all at this moment?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You just talked about, I think you were explaining the organisation as the -- let me just check that. Are you a war invalid?

utterances.speaker: JOSKO BABACIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for the answers, Mr. Babacic. Is there any need to put further questions to the witness? Then, Mr. Babacic, this concludes your testimony. I would like to thank you very much for having come to the videolink room and for having answered the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench. You are excused but I would like to instruct you, that if you see anyone during this day who has come to the same place to give testimony that you should not speak to that person. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then thank you, and I wish you a safe return home. Madam Registrar, the witness may leave the videolink room.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the representative of the registry in Zagreb escort the next witness into the courtroom. I do understand that that would be Radoslav Juricev Sudac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Will do, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Before you give evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require that you make a solemn declaration, that you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The text will now you handed out to you by the representative of the registry. May I invite to you make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. I took it from what we see on our screen and what we hear that you can see me and that you can hear me in a language that you understand. Could you please confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll first be examined by Mr. Misetic. Mr. Misetic is counsel for Mr. Gotovina. Mr. Misetic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Would you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: My name is Radoslav Juricev Sudac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if you could please show the witness Exhibit D193, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Juricev Sudac, do you see the statement in front of you?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall giving a statement to a representative of the Gotovina Defence on the 12th of May, 2008?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And in the bottom right-hand corner of that statement, is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Have you had a chance to review the statement before coming to court today?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Are there any changes or additional information that need to be included in this statement?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: At the time you gave this statement on the 12th of May, 2008, did you give it to the best of your knowledge and in accordance with the truth?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: I still had a very good knowledge, and I spoke only the truth and the whole truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If I asked you the same questions today in court that you were asked on the 12th of May, 2008, would you provide the same answers today in court that you provided in this witness statement, dated the 12th of May, 2008?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I move to admit into evidence Exhibit D193. MS. DE LANDRI: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, a number has already been assigned. That is number D193. MS. DE LANDRI: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. D193 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Juricev Sudac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, that concludes my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Juricev Sudac, you will now be cross-examined by counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you ready, Ms. De Landri, to cross-examine the witness? MS. DE LANDRI: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. MS. DE LANDRI: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Mr. Sudac, I would like to direct your attention to paragraph 4 of your statement. Do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Okay. In paragraph 4, you refer to -- I believe I just want to clarify. It's a -- the -- you say: "The tank with which we had some engine problems (village Pavasovici) T-34 didn't set out. The tank T-55, that was under my personal command, was located at the starting point ..." And then in the next full sentence you refer to --

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Jankova kuca.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: -- you refer to a third tank which you also call T-55. Is that an error?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: No, it's not. There were two tanks. T-55 and one T-34 tank. Each tank had a three-member crew, and my tank had a four-member crew, because I was its first member, its commander. The commander of the crew.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Maybe it's just a typographical error but in the way that it's written in paragraph 4 in the English translation, it refers to a third tank. Were there three tanks there on August 5th or two?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Yes. There were three tanks on my defence line. Two T-55 and one T-34. But the last one was not in a good working order.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. Directing your attention to paragraph 5. In paragraph 5, you've stated: "I know [sic] every man who was with me. I am certain ... Vladimir Gojanovic was neither assigned to me nor that he was driving in my tank. I am certain ... he was not [sic] in the tank at Gornje Bicane either." Can you tell the Chamber how you know Vladimir Gojanovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: As a resident of the county of Sibenik, I met many people. I have moved quite a lot. In the homeland war, I got to know him by sight. I never got engaged in a conversation with him, but I knew him by sight as a person. And as for your question, he was not assigned to me to that unit because I would know him, and we would have talked. The gentleman who brought the unit, Mr. Zafranovic did not bring Gojanovic with him. Gojanovic was not there. He never drove on my of my tanks. He was never in any of my tanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: When was the last time you saw Mr. Gojanovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: The last time I saw Mr. Gojanovic was in Plodine shop in Vodice, on the 27th of November, last year, in 2008.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And prior to August or September of 1995, when would have been the last time you saw him before then?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: In 1995, I did not see him that often. I worked in the Croatian Army as an officer. I did not have much time. My working hours were from 7.00 in the morning to 4.00 in the afternoon. I had a lot of work to do. I had a large family, and I spent most of the free time in my home in Vodice, so I did not really see him that often. I only learned that him and Mr. Petric took some money from my association, and the late Bozo asked me to go to their house to retrieve our money; but that hasn't happened to this day. We did not find them there. We returned. I never saw him after that until the 27th of November, last year, in Vodice.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Can you tell me in connection with your training in the army, did you ever receive a booklet on conduct in accordance with the Geneva Conventions?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Of course, we received those as officers. You're talking about a small white booklet containing all the rules. All of us officers and soldiers were well-informed and were aware of the Geneva Conventions. We were provided with instructions that we then on -- conveyed to our soldiers as to how to help a wounded or an imprisoned soldier. I exchanged three imprisoned enemy soldiers for our two dead soldiers. We did it together with UNPROFOR. There is a proof, documentary proof of that. Those white booklets were also distributed before Operation Storm across all units, all officers, non-commissioned officers, company commanders. So as far as that knowledge is concerned, we were all well-informed.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Well, try to confine your answers to your experience now. Tell me, if you can, as best you can recall, when you received the booklet that you're describing.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: I received the booklet even before Operation Storm. I was an officer who was in charge of the training of younger soldiers, and I was duty-bound to inform them about military rules. The first time I received that booklet, as an officer, was in 1993, or, rather, in 1992, in the month of November. That was the first time when I ever set my eyes on that booklet. At first, their shape was narrow and long, and later on they were replaced by those white booklets. I can still picture the cover drawing in my head with two soldiers. I'm no longer with the army. I have been retired for five years, and that image is fading in my memory, but I can still remember it.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Can you tell us the substance of what was in the booklet?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Yes. That booklet contained a lot of rules as to what you were supposed to do and what you were not allowed to do. How to administer first aid to wounded or imprisoned soldiers according to the Geneva Conventions, how to treat such soldiers, what to do with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Can you be more specific than that? Can you tell us the substance of the rules?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: The substance of the rules was this: Such a soldier should not be tortured, slaughtered, executed, abused, ill-treated. You should treat such soldiers in a humane way.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Is there any other substance you recall today?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Yes. For example, that you are not supposed to destroy churches, religious or -- buildings, that those should not be destroyed. There was a lot, but this is what I can remember. And I remember what our superior officers were telling us. It was a war and we remembered the most important things. Don't kill, don't loot, don't rape, help all those who are wounded. Such basic things.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Okay. Just ... I'd like to direct your attention to exhibit -- Defence Exhibit 205. And would you take a moment to read paragraph 2, please, the numbered paragraph 2. And just I'd like to direct your attention to --

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: -- direct your attention to the date, which, I think we can agree, is August 12th; is that right? And on the second page, the order is signed by Commander Kotlar. Are you familiar with him?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Of course, Danijel Kotlar, the commander who arrived from Zadar was the commander of the 113th Brigade. Of course. He was our main commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Can you tell me if you personally observed during Operation Storm any burning, looting, destruction of civilian property?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Since I was an artillery man [as interpreted], a tank would always be at the forefront. Our forces advanced and the artillery liberated the area. The tanks then moved on together with the infantry. What was happening behind us, I don't know. I know that the houses were burning, but it was somebody else who did that. It was not the troops who did that because our troops were strictly forbidden from doing any such thing. Our troops were strictly informed about all the facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we could check the interpretation with the witness of the first sentence of his answer. I'm not sure it was accurately recorded -- or interpreted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, Ms. De Landri asked you whether you personally observed during Operation Storm any burning, looting, destruction of civilian property. And you started your answer by saying: "Since I was ..." And could you, then, please repeat what you then said? Since you were a ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was on a tank. I was moving. I advanced together with my troops. I don't know whether there was any house burning. It was not my troops who did that. In any case, there was no looting. There was no setting houses on fire when we were advancing. I would not allow my troops to do such things as their commander. I would never allow them -- allow them to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you say, since I was an infantry man or an artillery man? Or what did you say in the beginning of your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I was a tank commander. I was on a tank and I progressed. I advanced. The artillery did their own thing and the tanks were at the forefront of the advance, and they were the ones who were paving the way and liberating the areas in front of the troops.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. Could I invite you to slow down your speed of speech so that the interpreters have sufficient time to translate what you say and that the transcribers have sufficient time to write it down. MS. DE LANDRI: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. De Landri, you may proceed. MS. DE LANDRI: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Just to return to the exhibit, Defence Exhibit 205. Do you know why Commander Kotlar would have issued that order, and specifically the substance in paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Because Mr. Kotlar received such an order from his superior, and that's how things go. And he just passed the order down to us lower-ranking officers, in order for the war to go on in a correct, composed, and fair manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Do you know someone by the name of Nikola Rasic? Rasic, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Yes, I know Mr. Nikola Rasic. We met sometime in October in Vodice, when my first commander of the -- independent company Boban Juricev Sudac brought him. That gentleman, I believe, was from Bosnia and he moved to Tribun [phoen] because his wife was from there. Or maybe they returned to Tribun to live there, I don't know. In any case, he arrived to train us because we were not very well-informed about all the weapon, and especially the rifle-mounted grenades. That training lasted 10 days. There were some 20 of us who underwent that training, maybe 25 of us. I'm not entirely sure. But I know that a lot of us did not complete the training and that only very few of us rained in training until the very end.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: You testified you met him in October. October of which year would that have been?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: In 1991, I believe, at the very beginning of the homeland war, I would say. After the liberation of the Sibenik bridge, that's when he arrived and joined our company.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And was that company a special forces unit?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: No. That unit was an element of the 3rd Battalion, or an integral part thereof. The late Ante Juric Boban was the commander of our 3rd Battalion of the 2nd Company of the independent company. The independent company for Vodice. The Sibenik bridge was occupied at the time. That's why we established a company consisting of volunteers from Vodice. He was in charge of our company. He is deceased and Rasic moved to Slavonia, and I believe that he currently resides there. MS. DE LANDRI: I would like to direct the witness's attention to the -- 65 ter number is 7394, and the ERN number is E3346837, and ...

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Do you have that document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: MS. DE LANDRI: The ERN number is 03346837.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Do you have that document in front of you, sir? Is that -- do you have it in front of you now, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Okay. You see that's a statement given by Nikola Rasic to the police in Zadar-Knin on October 12th, 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just as a technical matter before the witness answers, it is not a statement of the witness. It's an Official Note of the interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's a technical difference between a statement and an Official Note. If you would use the word "Official Note." Now, if we have verified that this is the document in front of the witness, then there might be no need to ask him what the document says and what we can read ourselves; that is, about dates. Of course, unless you wanted to verify that he really has this document in front of him. But, yes, you may proceed. MS. DE LANDRI: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Directing your attention to page 3 of the document. In particular, the section where your name appears. Do you see your name there?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Is that your name?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And is there a reference to your belonging to a special forces unit that Mr. Rasic was in?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Well, let me explain this to you, what is stated here. Every company, brigade, or battalion always consisted of soldiers who were abler soldiers and were more motivated to defend their country, and not everyone was capable of waging a war.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter notes that there was a break in the witness's answer. Can he be asked to repeat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Juricev, could you please repeat your answer because the interpreters could not follow every word. Perhaps you -- you said: "Every company, brigade, or battalion always consisted of soldiers who were more able -- abler soldiers and were more motivated to defend their country, and not everyone was ..." And what did you then say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were better trained and better at handling weapons. That's why we had the gentleman called Zec, i.e., Nikola Rasic. He was the one who taught us how to fire grenades from rifles. These were rifle launchers. We practiced with live ammunition. We would fire, launch a hand-grenade or a rifle grenade at old household appliances, et cetera, so we would not impact or the effect of the rifle grenade was. We would mount the grenade on a rifle and fire it. This sort of training took place over the course of 15 days. We had to learn how to work our way through difficult terrain, woods, wading through water. We had fitness exercises, and we had to go through all these drills with Zec, who was a professionally trained soldier.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Do you know why the term "dirty dozen" was used to refer to this special unit?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Well, the expression "dirty dozen" came into usage after I left. On the 29th of October, 1991, I joined an armoured mechanised company of the 113th Brigade, as soon as the first tank reached Vodice.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Can you tell me when was the last time that you spoke with Mr. Zafranovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: I spoke to him the last time in the Plodine shop on the 27th -- or, rather, that was just before the Christmas Day and the New Year's Eve. I think it was roughly around the 27th of December, rather than November. That was last year, and we met just before the Christmas Day, we were doing Christmas shopping. And I don't know why he mentioned my name at all and mentioned that he was part of my tank crew when he was not.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Did you -- did the two of you discuss the statements that you gave in connection with this case?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe there's some confusion with the witness and I don't believe he understood -- understood the name that was posed in the last question, so I believe you might want to clear that up. MS. DE LANDRI: Okay. I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you -- would you please do that. MS. DE LANDRI: -- do that with the next question. Thank you. Just one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I, at the same time, ask you how much time you'd still need, because we are already beyond the time we usually have a break. If it would be a matter of just a couple of minutes, then it's fine. If not, then we would have the break first. MS. DE LANDRI: Just a few moments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: MS. DE LANDRI: Now, I want to go back to the earlier question that I had asked the witness, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: My question was, and is, have you been in contact with Mr. Zafranovic.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: I was in contact with Mr. Zafranovic. I asked him why it was that he mentioned my name, first and last name, and said that he was with me on my tank when he did not take part in Storm at all. MS. DE LANDRI: Mr. President, one procedural matter. The document that I had been asking the witness about, it is actually an exhibit, D1540. That was the police interview. I just want that to be clear for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the Official Note so you will not tender it. It's already in evidence. MS. DE LANDRI: Right, thank you. I don't have any further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, any questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber would like to read again the document which is on our screen before we make up our mind as to whether we have any questions for the witness, but that would take too long. Therefore, you are not yet excused. Then it may that be we have some questions for you after the break; that's not certain yet. So would you please remain there, and after the break we will inform you whether there are any further questions or whether your testimony is concluded. We'll have a break, and we'll resume at five minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Juricev, I have a few questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You told us about the booklets that you received, an early version already quite some years before Operation Storm, and then, later, it was a different format. You told us that officers and non-commissioned officers would receive that. Were they supposed, then, to instruct the soldiers, or did the soldiers get their own copies of those booklets? What happened?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Since the commanders of platoons, companies, and squads received such booklets, the soldiers were familiar with them. They would be photocopied, and they would receive instructions. Besides, soldiers were told about the rules of war in -- during that training.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You say they were photocopied. There was not a sufficient number of booklets to be distributed among all the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: An Official Note was shown to you, in which it is described how you were selected to become a member of a special unit. And I think you told us that you received some training. You told us about grenades fired by rifles. How long did you stay in that unit or -- if it was a real unit?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: I spent a short period of time in that unit only, because I became a part of the tank crew on the 28th of October, 1991, which is the date when the first tank arrived in Vodice; this is something that I've already said. I was, therefore, a member of that unit -- no, sorry, it was on the 29th of March. Wait. On the 18th of October, there was the capture. It was on the 29th of November that I went to join that unit, whereas, on the 18th of November, we captured three enemy soldiers in the village of Cista Velika, and it was the first such instance of us having prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we are talking about what year at this moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So only for a very short period of time you were a member of that group or unit.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: A very short period only. That particular unit existed for as long as late Ante Juricev Boban was alive. As far as I remember, it ceased to exist subsequently, and Mr. Zec left the unit later on. Subsequently, two smaller units were formed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You testified today that you knew that houses were burning but that you were moving forward in your tank and that you knew for sure that it could not have been members of your army that would have set fire to those houses because they were prohibited to do that. Now, do you have any explanation as to how these houses were put on fire? What -- do you know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: I am very poorly informed of these events. It was summertime, and whenever a tracer bullet was fired, it was quite possible for it to set hay or grass on fire. The situation was such that there was always an exchange of fire, it was highly flammable, and there was always a high possibility for a haystack or a hay barn to be set on fire in the process. My soldiers were never allowed to act without my command, without my orders, and I fought honourably and honestly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're talking about your unit. Could you exclude for the possibility instead -- for the possibility that other HV members may have set houses on fire or may have looted or intentionally destroyed civilian property?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, nobody did that sort of thing in my unit. I only remember in relation to Varivode, that there was some men who were part of my group when we were undergoing training. I know what they did, and I know that there was disciplinary punishment passed down against them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to ask you a few questions about -- about your interview. Could you tell us how you were approached prior to giving -- to have given your statement in 2008, in May? Did you receive a phone call, did someone come to your house, was it the first time that you were approached? Could you give us a bit more details?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: My first contact was with the president of the association of invalids, Josko Babacic, who told me that Mr. Misetic's team would come there on behalf of the Defence for General Gotovina. I volunteered to provide a statement, if they would wish so, on their arrival. And they arrived on the 17th of May, unless I'm mistaken. That was when I gave my statement. And that was my first contact and encounter with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you have not attended a meeting some years before in 2006?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, about your statement, did Mr. Babacic tell you what -- what the issue was for which your statement would be important?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: He didn't tell me anything. I didn't know what the team of lawyers would tell me either, until we finally met and until they showed me why it was that they were seeking to speak to me. They showed it to me on their laptop. When I saw that Vladimir Gojanovic gave a false statement, I said that I had to confirm and say what I had to say personally, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When did they show you the -- was it a video of Mr. Gojanovic's testimony? What was it that they had shown you on the laptop?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: I only saw his statement when he said in The Hague that he was the one who had prevented the Croatian Army from committing genocide on the Serbs and that he would testify against Croatia and the Generals. I lied. I can guarantee 100 per cent that he was not with me, and I have to tell you that we were an army that prevented any sort of genocide from being committed against the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I would like to hear more details about what you saw. Was this a video, first of all?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Well, yes, it was the ordinary video footage. I'm not quite sure what it was. I'm not quite familiar with that sort of video. But I do recall seeing Gojanovic testify in The Hague, in the courtroom in the The Hague. I saw it on TV.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I hear of two things: First, you said that you were shown a video in which Mr. Gojanovic said he would testify in The Hague, as you said, against ...

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: That he testified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just see what you -- what is on the transcript of what you said. Yes, you said and I read one of your answers. You said: "I only saw his statement when he said in The Hague that he was the one who had prevented the Croatian Army from committing genocide on the Serbs and that he would testify against Croatia and the Generals." Now that is a bit of a confusing answer because it says when -- it says that --

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: That he testified against the Generals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was this shown to you before you gave your statement?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, when, then, did they show this to you?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: They had the footage on their laptop. The team of lawyers showed me on their laptop that he had testified in The Hague against the Generals. He said that he had been with me on the tank. So they first had questions for me and then they showed it to me, and I told them that he was not with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was that on the same day when you gave your statement, that they had shown it to you?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: It was after a while that I saw the footage. I gave my statement, and then I was shown the footage and asked whether I knew the individual. I know him, and I know that he was not with me on the tank.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that was on the same day that you gave your statement that the video was shown to you?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When did you become aware that your testimony was specifically focussing on whether -- that your interview would focus on Mr. Gojanovic, his role, in Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: The odds were not 100 per cent that I would be testifying but they wanted to confirm with me whether Gojanovic was telling the truth or not. And then later, it was through a set of coincidences that I ended up finally appearing before the Tribunal. And they told me that I should only tell the truth, whether he was there or he was not there, and I can confirm that he was not with me on the tank.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did Mr. Babic tell you that it was about the role of Mr. Gojanovic that there was a need to interview you?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: We were not 100 percent sure but he told me that I should be prepared and that I could possibly be summoned by The Hague, by the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was not my question. My question was whether Mr. Babacic told you prior to your interview that it was about -- whether Mr. Gojanovic had told the truth, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: It didn't have to do with -- with Gojanovic telling the truth or not. It had to do with the statement that he gave in The Hague. I was supposed to confirm whether he was, indeed, with me on the tank or not, and that was how Josko and I then knew later on what -- what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was Josko - that's Mr. Babacic - present when you were interviewed?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Out of the team of lawyers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I'm just asking whether he was present during your interview. You were interviewed?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Josko was present. He was the one who called me, and he was the one through whom I got to meet the team of lawyers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But was he present when you were interviewed? So, first of all, do you remember who interviewed you, who put the questions to you when you gave your statement?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: There were three members of the Defence team which were sent by Mr. Misetic. There was Stomo [phoen], there was the late gentleman, and the third one. I don't even know their names, to be honest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So when you say there were three persons, do you mean to say three persons apart from you?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: There were three lawyers, members of Mr. Misetic's team. The Defence team representing Mr. Ante Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is when you were interviewed. You're talking about that interview?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, was Mr. Babacic also present, apart from the three lawyers?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you given any statement by Mr. Gojanovic to read? Did you read any statement given by Mr. Gojanovic, or was just the video shown to you?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: First of all, I saw it on TV. I saw his false testimony. And I was appalled when I saw that. Knowing Gojanovic, I immediately remembered what sort of criminal he was. First he stole money from my association, the association of Croatian veterans of the Croatian war of the city of Vodice. He stole that money through his own account. To this very day, he has not returned that money, and I immediately knew what the whole matter was about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it after you had seen his testimony on television that you were approached by Mr. Babacic; or was it already before you had seen this on television?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: After. I already seen him on TV, and some 20 days after that, Josko called me and told me that I should present myself to provide a statement. I asked him who was coming, and he said, The team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, what you saw on television, I just want to be sure about that. Was it a kind of an interview Mr. Gojanovic gave, or was it really his testimony in a courtroom in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: What I saw was his testimony in the courtroom, in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us, Mr. Gojanovic, is he average height? Is he a very tall man? Is he a small man? Could you tell us -- could you describe him?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Gojanovic is a tall person, heavily built. He weighs 120 to 130 kilos. He has short hair. His head is round. I know him personally. His brother was a member of the 113th Brigade. He was with the signals company. He was a signals man. I know his brother personally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. Could we just switch off the speaker in Zagreb for a second? I think that can be visible on the screen. If you would wait for a second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question, if I may? Hello?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask you something? Hello.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you do that at a later moment, yes? Microphone -- the witness now can't hear me anymore. One of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness then take his earphones off. Are the parties aware of any testimony given by Mr. Gojanovic, other than on the 16th and 18th of May, 2008?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: We have 16 and 19 of May and we are not aware of anything, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I believe also in my records here he started on the 15th, if I'm not mistaken so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But after the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because I would like to put that to the witness and I want to be sure that I did not make any mistake. Mr. Juricev, I extensively asked you questions about what you had seen as testimony of Mr. Gojanovic and that you were invited after that moment to give a statement. If I would tell you that Mr. Gojanovic testified in this court not before but after you had already given your statement on the 12th of May, would you have any explanation to that? Because your testimony clearly stated that Mr. Gojanovic -- you had seen him on television testifying in The Hague before you gave your statement; whereas, this Chamber and the parties do agree that it was only after you'd given your statement that Mr. Gojanovic could have appeared on television giving testimony in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: No, I don't know who made a mistake. I saw him on TV. And then the team of lawyers came from The Hague, and they asked me about that case, which means thereafter. I provided my statement after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. I have no further questions. Any questions? MS. DE LANDRI: Yes, just one briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. De Landri has a short question for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Mr. Sudac, you gave your statement -- your written statement on May 12th, 2008, and according to the document it was conducted by, and you will pardon my pronunciation if I mispronounce, Jozo Ribicic; is that right? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: In response to Judge Orie's questions, you referred to an interview that was conducted by three members of the Defence team. When was that conducted?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: When that gentleman, Jozo Ribicic, was there, he signed the document, and I did as well. And two more men came with him. Him and two more people came.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And were there two separate interviews or just one interview?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: Just one.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And are their names indicated on this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOSLAV JURICEV SUDAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Juricev, you earlier said that you would like to ask me a question, although it is uncommon for a witness to ask questions, I, nevertheless, would allow you to ask what you want to ask. I'm not promising that I will answer your question. I'll first wait and hear what you wanted to ask.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to make a correction. I saw Mr. Gojanovic on the 27th of December, between Christmas and New Year and that was in 2008. I wanted to make that correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you can take that into account, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would like to thank you as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is on the record. This concludes your testimony, Mr. Juricev. Mr. Juricev Sudac. And I would like to thank you for coming to the videolink room and for having answered the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench.
