Could I ask the representative of the registry to escort the witness out of the courtroom. And, at the same time -- but first, I'd like to instruct you, Mr. Juricev Sudac. If there are any other people in the premises where you are at present and who still may have to testify, you should not speak to them. Neither should you speak to anyone who has already testified today. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the representative of the registry not only escort Mr. Juricev Sudac out of the room but also escort Mr. Zafranovic into that same room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Mr. Zafranovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you also see us in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you given evidence, I would like to invite you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is now handed out to you by Madam Registrar. Could you please make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please, be seated, Mr. Zafranovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zafranovic, you will first briefly be examined by Mr. Misetic. Mr. Misetic is counsel for the Prosecution -- for the -- for Mr. Gotovina. I apologise, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No offence taken, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Zafranovic. Would you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning. My name is Davor Zafranovic. My late father's name is Joso.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if we could show the witness Exhibit D203, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zafranovic, do you recall giving a statement to a representative of the Gotovina Defence on the 12th of May, 2008?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And looking at the statement in front of you, is that the statement that you signed on the 12th of May, 2008?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Is that your signature on the -- in the lower right-hand corner of the first page?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Have you had a chance to review this statement before coming to the Tribunal's office in Zagreb today?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the day before yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And do any changes need to be made to the statement or any additional information added to the statement?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: I would just like to add that Sudac, the head of the tank crew, that we did what he said. Sometimes we went behind the tank, sometimes we went in front of the tank, and sometimes we travelled on the tank itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Other than that information, is the statement accurate to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: At the time you gave this statement to the Gotovina Defence, did you give it to the best of your knowledge and in accordance with the truth?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, my whole life is nothing but the truth, and I speak only the truth and only what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Is that then, yes, that you gave a statement to the best of your knowledge and in accordance with the truth?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If I asked you the same questions today in court that you were asked on the 12th of May, 2008, would your answers today in court be the same as the answers you provided in your witness statement that is in front of you right now?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they would be identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I move for the admission into evidence of Exhibit D203. MS. DE LANDRI: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D203 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zafranovic, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, that concludes my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Misetic. Mr. Zafranovic, you will now be cross-examined by Ms. De Landri. Ms. De Landri is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed. MS. DE LANDRI: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Mr. Zafranovic, you gave your statement in May of 2008; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And your statement related to events that occurred in August of 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And in the approximately 13 years that elapsed, did you discuss those events with anyone?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you know, whenever I meet with my commanders, in the past, we did tell stories; but as time goes on, we meet less and less, and we don't talk as much.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Well, let me direct your attention to the statement itself and to some of the individuals you identify in the statement. Did you discuss the specifics of the statement with anyone in that time-frame? I realize it's a very broad time-frame but ...

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was last year when we discussed this event at somewhat greater length, when Sudac and I provided our statements, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And when you say, When Sudac and I provided the statements, can you describe the circumstances of -- of when you provided your statements?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: A representative of the Defence came to see us, and we were taken to a room, just him and I, I believe that you will find it in here. I gave my statement in the presence of that person. I don't know if it was Misetic or somebody else. I don't know who it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: When you say - you said "us." Who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Just Sudac and myself were there, and Mr. Babacic. In the other room I mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: During the time that you gave your statement, Sudac and Mr. Babic [sic] was present?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Mischaracterises the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see the point you would like to further explore but you can do it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we get an answer anyhow. If you, please, would further explore who was where, at what time so that we get full information. Please proceed. MS. DE LANDRI: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: When you went to give your statement in this matter back in May of 2008, you went with Sudac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: No. When I provided my statement, it was just me and the lawyer. Prior to that, I was with the others, but during the actual statement, it was just the two of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Thank you. When you say "the others," who were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Sudac was in a different room, in the other room, and he was waiting there to be called to provide his statement after me.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Where did this take place?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: In the HVIDRA of Sibenik.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And did the two of you travel to that building together?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I came by boat from Prvic, and from the harbour, I came to that building on foot.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: When you went to the -- when you went to give the statement, did you know that he was also coming to give a statement on the same day?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know, but I assumed.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Why did you assume he was coming to give a statement at the same time?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Why did I assume? Because the operation involved the tank crew headed by Vucanin [phoen]. There was myself and four or five other combatants. We were either on the tank or around the tank.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And who contacted you and asked you to give a statement?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: I was aware of the statement, that Sibenik mentioned my name I knew what that was all about. I knew that Gojanovic had testified, and I was contacted by Babacic, I believe. I believe that he called me.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: When you say "Babacic," who are you referring to? Can you give us a first name?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: I call him Babacic. I know his name. I believe that his name is Jole, but I really can't be sure. I know his name, but I can't remember. Jole, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: So were you interviewed after Mr. Gojanovic had testified in the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But my name was already mentioned in newspapers and on Radio Sibenik by that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And can you tell us in what regard your name was mentioned in the newspapers and on the radio?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: To be honest, I don't listen to Radio Sibenik. My sister told me that my name had been mentioned on the radio. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: What -- what did she or anyone else tell you about what was said about you on the radio?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that reference was made to Petric and Gojanovic and then they mentioned me as a witness of genocide or, rather, of the way genocide was prevented. Something to that effect, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Well, just to direct your attention again to your written statement, and that's Exhibit D203. We can agree that the date that you gave that statement was May 12th, 2008. Is that right, Mr. Zafranovic?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Okay. And if I told you that Vladimir Gojanovic testified in the ICTY after that date, would you be able to explain the discrepancy?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Mind you, I wondered at Gojanovic mentioning my name at all. I was in Operation Storm, I was on a tank on the 5th of August of the year. And as for him testifying, I don't know if it was before or after.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention to paragraph 10 of your statement. Take a moment to look at that.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And it says on August 6th after we arrived in Bribir, we stayed there overnight. The next morning at daylight my company took a one-day rest. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: So on August 6th, you are -- you had a day off ; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it -- we didn't have the entire day off, but, for the most part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Okay. The next sentence says, We returned on August 7th. Can you recall what you did on August 7th?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 7th of August I was in prison, or, rather, in detention.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And tell us the circumstances that led up to your imprisonment.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: I can tell you about it. On the 6th, a friend came to see me. We call him Drobonj, but his last name is Slavica. He got me into his car and suggested that we visit our -- or, rather, that we go and collect the mortal remains of our friend, a fellow soldier. He said that he was one hand short, that he needed someone to give him a hand. We came close to Skradin, along a dirt road, and we found a hand, just a hand that had been burned. We placed it in an island bag and took it to the local cemetery. However, they would not agree at the local cemetery to bury the one hand, so we went to Gorica, and we made arrangements for the hand to be placed in a coffin so that my friend could receive a proper burial. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: You see, I was 53 at the time of the Storm, and I was a proper volunteer. I didn't receive a single call-up letter. This person, his name is Garma, he was ten years my junior, and he was closest to my age. All the other ones were kids for me, including those who took part in Operation Storm. So I befriended him. You see, I live on an island, and I was the president of the local commune of the island there before I joined Operation Storm. So I had to travel by boat and I arrived at 1530 there, and I planned on going back by boat again on the following morning, and I had all my weapons and my gear on me because I simply didn't have the time to drop them off in the barracks, and I wanted to show up there a bit early. So I wanted to be there early because I was their president. As I arrived down there, some 30 or some 40 of them joined us and we celebrated. We celebrated the Storm. So we stayed there until 12.30. We were in a restaurant in Punta whereupon we proceeded to a bar where they refused to serve us drinks. The barkeeper, the lady barkeeper, would not give us drinks. It was 12.45 and the bar was officially opened until 1.00, so it was 10 or 15 minutes before the closing time. I got angry. You see, throughout that time, from Bribir to Sibenik, wherever we stopped to have a drink, we would be served drinks. In Poljane, for instance, we were not only served drinks but we were greeted cordially and warmly by the ladies there as well, and you see, in my own home town I was there with some friends of mine from Split and from my fellow citizens of Prvic. We wouldn't be served drinks. So I went home, and I fired a burst of fire in the area because I had heard that the brother of the lady barkeeper was living nearby and was asleep, so I simply wanted to wake him up. That was all. I don't know what he was doing in Prvic. He was a senior officer of the police, and I suppose he was there on a holiday. So what he did then was that, when I went to bed, suddenly 17 policemen, some military, some civilian policemen, surrounded my house, would that they had been there together with us in Operation Storm rather than around my house [as interpreted]. So a police boat arrived and took me to Poljane into detention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. De Landri, could you, please --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My command learned of the developments -- MS. DE LANDRI:

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: I just want to direct your attention to a document and ask you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But -- MS. DE LANDRI: -- just about the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. MS. DE LANDRI: Oh. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. De Landri, would you please consider that the interpreters need sometime to translate especially if the witness is going very fast, and I would -- the Chamber would highly appreciate if would you focus the witness -- MS. DE LANDRI: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and intervene whenever necessary to take him back to what appears the most relevant things. MS. DE LANDRI: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. MS. DE LANDRI:

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Were you intoxicated at the time of your arrest on August 7th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, what do you mean? Well, I was tipsy. I wasn't drunk. I didn't resist them. I didn't get into -- pick up a fire [as interpreted] with them. I went with them, and I suppose --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch what the witness said last. MS. DE LANDRI:

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: My question was, were you intoxicated at the time of your arrest on August 7th, 1995? Just yes or no is sufficient.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. De Landri, the interpreters informed us that they did not catch the last words of the witness. The proper way is to ask the witness to repeat those last words, not to have them disappear from the record -- MS. DE LANDRI: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but putting the question again and giving guidance to the witness that a yes or a no would do, which, in view of his earlier answer, must seem to be clear already. Mr. Zafranovic, you earlier said that you -- you went with the police officers, and you said: "And I suppose ..." and then your words are missing. Could you repeat what you said when you said: "And I suppose." You suppose what? I'm not seeking a long story but just what you said earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was asked if I had been drunk, and my answer was, had I been drunk, I would have resisted them. They would not have arrested me as easily as that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. MS. DE LANDRI: I would like to direct the witness's attention to 65 ter 7345. And the ERN number, the first number is 04249656.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: I would like to direct your attention to paragraph 4. Can you just take a look at that briefly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be provided with a hard copy. Ms. De Landri, could you repeat the number for the -- MS. DE LANDRI: Oh, certainly. It's -- the first page of document is 04249656. And the paragraph I want to direct the witness's attention to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first try and find the document. If you look at your screen, you will see what happens in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think if we can assist I believe it is 65 ter 7395. MS. DE LANDRI: That's right. That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. De Landri confirms that that's the right number. Ms. De Landri, it's now the time to guide the witness to the relevant -- MS. DE LANDRI:

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: I would just like to direct your attention to paragraph 4 of the document. Have you had an opportunity to review it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. De Landri, I take it that the witness needs a bit more time, because I not even have read the paragraph. MS. DE LANDRI:

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Okay. Have you had an opportunity to review the document, sir? Not the document, excuse me, paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Okay. And does that refresh your memory about the event of August 7th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Most of what is stated here is false. It wasn't 1.05; it was 12.45. The bar should not have closed yet. Second, how it is that she can possibly know that I was under the influence of alcohol. I may have been excited, I may have been exhilarated since we had successfully done the first part of Storm. MS. DE LANDRI: May I interrupt the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MS. DE LANDRI:

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Okay. The part of the statement that says that you fired some 15 bullets into the air, and broke three tables, two chairs, two ceiling lights, is that accurate, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: It was a burst of fire, not 15 rounds but over 25. And as for the chairs and tables, they were not broken.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Okay. And just -- you were later arrested, is it 4.00 a.m. in the morning? Is that accurate? Several hours later?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if was 3.00 or 4.00. I had already gone to bed, and I was asleep.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Okay. You were arrested at your home. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm telling you that I was asleep.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And that was on August 7th; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the 7th.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And how long --

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 7th of August, yes, night-time.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And how long did you remain in custody?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: 24 hours. MS. DE LANDRI: I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Any questions in re-examination, Mr. Misetic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zafranovic, I would like to know a bit more details about who approached you before you gave a statement in May 2008.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that it was Babacic who told me over the phone that I should come to HVIDRA on such and such a day, at such and such an hour. I think it was Babacic, Jole Babacic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, did he tell you why your statement was needed?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I had already presumed, since this was already discussed, it was general knowledge in the town. There was no need for him to give me any explanations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What was general knowledge in the town?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, only that Gojanovic was a witness of The Hague Tribunal and that he mentioned me and Sudac as witnesses substantiating his testimony, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said he mentioned you. Do you mean to say that he mentioned your name in The Hague; or that he mentioned your name elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't know the details. I know that my friends called me and told me that they had heard my name mentioned on Radio Sibenik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You earlier told us about your sister. You're now telling us about your friends. Could you tell us who those friends were and were they, in addition to your sister, telling you that your name was --

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, my sister normally listens to the radio. She is now 80. I don't know how old she was at the time. And she always listens to the radio early on in the morning; I don't. So it was my sister who phoned me about it. There was another friend who is Gojanovic's neighbour. He lives just next door to Gojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So they told you that Gojanovic had mentioned your name. What was your reaction to that? How did you feel about that?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: I know Gojanovic's late father very well. Frankly, I don't know him. I probably saw him before, but I did see him afterwards, after him giving the statement, and I know now that he is quite corpulent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was, what did you feel about Gojanovic mentioning your name?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Since not a single case smacking of genocide was something that I ever witnessed during Storm, it did not really worry me, did not cause me any concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you have any other concern; or were you just convinced that he didn't tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, the 10 or 15 days that I spent during Storm, I met an enormous amount of people at the very start, on the 5th, some of the people I used to know I met in Gracac. Then some people that I went to see because I knew that they stayed there, or their mothers, like the Dragovic individual, then in Srb and in the surrounding villages. I even gathered some 15 or 16 Serb civilians who were there and gave them food, and this is something that I remember fondly. I asked them, Why didn't all of you leave since everybody else left? And do you know what an old lady told me? Dear sir, we are the wretched poor and they wouldn't take us them with them. On the second day, that same old lady told me when I asked her, Why aren't you eating anything, you have lambs and other food, because you see I brought them some lambs that I found. She told me, Comrade, this belongings to other persons. So I was 53. And what sort of a fool would I be to allow anyone to mistreat or kill those people?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could it that be Mr. Gojanovic had seen things you had not seen?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Since, according to what he says, he was on the same tank that I was on as a -- I think as a lance corporal or something, and I never saw him, I don't know what gives him the right to talk about Oluja and his -- Storm and his participation therein.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did he not participate in Storm, or did he?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: That's something that HVIDRA and those people there would know. But as far as I'm concerned, he was not there on that day with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I'd like to go back to you giving your statement. You were told what Mr. Gojanovic -- or at least what was heard on the radio by your friends. So what did you conclude from that, as far as the subject of your statement would be? Do you expect it to be about Mr. Gojanovic; or just about the events in Storm you participated in? What was your impression at the time?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: As I told you before, I didn't give Gojanovic any thought. I had an idea that I would be giving my experience in Storm, and I can tell you that nothing resembling genocide ever occurred there. As for the setting houses on fire and looting of cattle, I can tell that you it was somebody else other than Croatian soldiers who did that. We were busy. We had our tasks. And, besides, we were also afraid. We were not professional soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I stop you there? When you went to the -- did Mr. Babacic tell you where to go and when?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean last year or now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Last year.

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: He only told me to come to the HVIDRA building. And then we went to the notary public's office, and we signed our statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did he know the time you had to be in the HVIDRA building?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. He told me to come on the first boat. However, I didn't catch the first but a later boat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you speak with any former members of your unit before you gave your statement?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: I told you that I reside on a small island just off the coast of Sibenik, and information does not reach us as easily as they -- as it does in town. It was in the middle of the tourist season and I had my hands full of other things, and I didn't really occupy myself with all sorts of stories that I heard, or could tell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Once you arrived in the building, did you speak with anyone about the statement, other than to the person that interviewed you?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. Not only that I think that, I'm sure that I didn't. As soon as I arrived there, I was taken to -- to a different room, and the rest stayed in the other room. They closed a door behind me, and I provided my statement there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said: "... the rest stayed in the other room." Who was the rest?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Babacic, Sudac Juricev, the tank man, and I don't know if there was anybody else from HVIDRA. There was another person, but I don't remember who he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you were interviewed in this room, was there anyone else than you and the person that interviewed you?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so, no. It was his explicit request that there should be just him and me. I was surprised to hear that. I thought that maybe we could all be together, but he insisted it was just him and me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you ever see a video in relation with Mr. Gojanovic's testimony?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You didn't see it on television?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: I saw him once on a programme called On Sunday at 2.00, when the anchor, called Stankovic, interviewed him. And to be honest with you, he looked like a imbecile to me, not like a normal intelligent person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you watch this programme after you had given your statement or prior to giving your statement, in 2008?

utterances.speaker: DAVOR ZAFRANOVIC
utterances.text: That was subsequently. And what appalled me the most, and that's why I'm telling that he looked like a imbecile, when he said that him and Petric established an association under the title "The Truth About the Homeland War," and that the name-sake association existed in Bosnia and in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. The reason why you considered him to look like a imbecile are not of such relevance that we would continue with that. I have no further questions for you. Have the questions by the Bench triggered any need to put further questions to the witness? Mr. Zafranovic, this concludes your testimony. I would like to thank you very much for coming to the videolink facility and for having answered all the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and I would like to wish you a safe trip home again. If could you just take off your earphones for a second. Madam Registrar, could you, perhaps when you escort Mr. Zafranovic out of the courtroom, could you please check whether Mr. Babacic is still on the premises or not, because we might consider to re-call him very briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Will do, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If he is still on the premises, could you please ask him to stay -- stand by. We will first have a break, and we resume at five minutes to 1.00, and then I take it you will report to us whether Mr. Babacic is still available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could Mr. Rak be escorted into the videolink room? Yes. Good afternoon, Mr. Rak. Before you give evidence, I would like to invite you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text will now be handed out to you by Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Rak, please be seated. Mr. Rak --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I take it that you can see us and that can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You will first be examined by Mr. Misetic. Mr. Misetic is counsel for Mr. Gotovina. Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Would you please state your name for the record.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: Dragan Rak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if we could, please, show the witness Exhibit D197, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rak, do you recall giving a statement to members of the Gotovina Defence on the 8th of May, 2008?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And looking through that document that you're now being shown, is that the statement that you signed on the 8th of May, 2008?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And is that your signature in the bottom right-hand corner of the first page?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Prior to coming to the Tribunal's field office in Zagreb today, did you have a chance to review the statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: When I provided it on the 8th of May, 2008, it was clearly read out to me. I read it myself, and I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Since then, have you had a chance to look at that statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And is the statement accurate, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: It is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you wish to make any changes or additions to your statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: At the time you gave the statement, did you give it to the best of your knowledge and in accordance with the truth?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If I asked you the same questions today in court that you were asked on the 8th of May, 2008, would you provide the same answers today in court that you provided in your signed witness statement of the 8th of May, 2008?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: I would, indeed, the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I move for the admission of D197 into evidence. MS. DE LANDRI: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D197 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rak, thank you for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, that concludes my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Misetic. Mr. Rak, you will now be cross-examined by Ms. De Landri. Ms. De Landri is counsel for the Prosecution. You may proceed, Ms. De Landri. MS. DE LANDRI: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Mr. Rak, how many men were under your command when you were in the 113th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And did you have a staff at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: A staff? A staff of a battalion? Yes, we had it in the Bribirski Knezovi barracks.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: How many men were on the staff?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: The battalion command comprised 14 men.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Can you name the 14 men?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: I don't remember their names.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: I want to direct your attention to the third full paragraph in your statement, and in particular the events of August 4th that you refer to. The statement refers to heavy enemy resistance, and -- pardon me. I just want to strike that. And it refers to an attack that you launched. Due to heavy enemy resistance, your attack deceased. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And at that time you had wounded soldiers and one dead soldier; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And you withdrew your soldiers to take care of your wounded; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that, under the circumstances, the welfare and safety of your men were uppermost in your mind?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: Yes, that was the most important thing on my mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And that would be true throughout all of Operation Storm, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Okay. Turning your attention to the events of August 5th, in the fourth full paragraph. You led a renewed attack, you say you organised quarters for your soldiers. Can you recall approximately how many soldiers there were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: On the entire axis, there were around 650 men altogether.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And turning to August 6th. What happened on August 6th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: The line reached in the village of Bribir. I billeted my unit. The accommodation or the soldiers who just arrived was provided. They arrived at the houses in Bribir. The soldiers were given time to rest, and then they went home.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Directing your attention to the last full paragraph of your statement, where, in particular, you refer to Vladimir Gojanovic. You state you know him personally from 1992 or 1993. How did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I met him at the Bribirski Knezovi barracks in 1992 or 1993. He was introduced to me by his brother Ivica Gojanovic, who was an officer of the Croatian Army, my colleague. I saw him wearing a uniform that conscripts wore and I concluded that, at the time, he was a conscript in the 113th Brigade. After that I never saw him again. I did not see him during Operation Storm or the time following Operation Storm while the unit was still in the theatre of war.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: You've described circumstances where you had a great deal of responsibility under a lot of stress. Would it be fair to say that you might not have been in a position to see all of the participants of Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: Of course. It was impossible to see everybody. It was impossible to be everywhere at every moment. But the period from the 3rd of August, 1995 to the 15th of September, 1995 is too long a time for me not to see him, if he had been there.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention to Court Exhibit 2. Sir, do you have that document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Take a look at the first page. And can you tell me whether or not that conflicts with your recollection about whether or not Vladimir Gojanovic was involved in the military during Operation Storm in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: I've not seen this before, and as far as I can remember, this does not correspond the truth. It is not true that this person, the person in question, was in my unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to doubt the authenticity of this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: As to who drafted the document and as to whether it is authenticate or not it is not up to me to say. This is down to a different body, the institution that issues such documents. I was just a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Well, could I direct your attention to the stamp on the bottom right-hand of the first page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If only the original and not the translation is shown on the screen, could we have then the original also on our manageable screens so that we can zoom in and out, if we want. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Talking about the English translation, there seems to be no English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: May I have the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Ask that the witness take his earphones off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Court will recall that this document came when Mr. Gojanovic, over a weekend, came to court, and the reason it's a court exhibit is he had it faxed from someone -- from a friend of his to his hotel here, I believe, and then tendered it as a court exhibit in evidence himself. So if we're going to get into questions of authenticity it traces back to Mr. Gojanovic himself. As far as I know, it didn't come from the Republic of Croatia directly, and the reason there is no translation is because it wasn't provided by one of the parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so The Chamber should have been -- I further find -- One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are some more puzzles in relation to this document. Please proceed. MS. DE LANDRI: Just to clarify a matter relating to the translation, there was some colloquy on the record at the time when Mr. Gojanovic first testified back in May of 2008, and counsel is correct, that he brought this document with him. There was a discussion on the record, I think, the page of the transcript was 3114 that the registry was going have the document translated. But in anticipation of asking some questions about the document, we provided a translation for counsel and the Court. And so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And where do I find it at this moment? MS. DE LANDRI: Oh, I'm sorry, Your Honour. It is right behind the original B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But I'm working electronically. MS. DE LANDRI: Oh, okay. It's ET --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm afraid that the Chamber has only access to documents that were exhibited and any attached translations but -- and I do not have my in e-court system any attached translation to this document. But perhaps Mr. Registrar is going to help us out. Perhaps meanwhile you already proceed and we'll wait for the assistance of the registrar. Oh, it's now on the screen. Yes, please proceed. MS. DE LANDRI: The witness, does he have his headphones on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has the witness been provided with a hard copy? Yes. Then please proceed. MS. DE LANDRI: He doesn't have his headset on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Yes, you're right. Please proceed. MS. DE LANDRI:

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Sir, my question to you was: Do you have any reason to doubt the authenticity of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It was asked and answered, Your Honour. MS. DE LANDRI: No, I'm afraid it wasn't answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll check in the transcript. One second, please. Yes, the witness answered that it's not for him to authenticate. The question, however, was whether there were any reasons for him to doubt the authenticity, which is not -- therefore, the answer is not a direct answer. You can ask the witness again. MS. DE LANDRI:

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Sir, do you have any reason, looking at this document here today, to doubt its authenticity?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: The document doesn't indicate any units. I doubt the authenticity of this document. My version of the truth and the truth is that this gentleman was not in my battalion during Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you some questions about the circumstances of your coming to testify here today and giving a statement. Who asked you to give your statement? Directing your attention back to May of 2008, who asked you to -- who originally approached you and asked you to give a statement in May of 2008?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: I was first approached by Josko Babacic. After that, gentleman came who testified my witness statement. We were in the same room, myself, Mr. Marin Ivanovic, and Mr. Jozo Ribicic.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And when was that that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: That was on the day when I provided my statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear, were you contacted in advance of the day that you provided your statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: Josko Babacic.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And when did that occur?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: That was -- I can't remember exactly. A couple of days prior to that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: MS. DE LANDRI:

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, can you tell us what he said to you when he first contacted you about this matter?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: He said that that gentleman from the General's Defence team would come, and that we would provide our statements about Operation Storm or, rather, about the truth of what happened during Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And what did you say in response?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: That he would call me when the gentleman arrived and that we would meet in the same rooms where I gave my statement to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Before you gave your statement, did anyone show you any documents related to the events that you were asked about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: So who was present when you gave your statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: Mr. Marin Ivanovic and Jozo Ribicic.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Okay. And what was the date?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: The 8th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And were you told what the statement was going to be used for?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: For the defence of the General.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Any more specifically, were you told what the statement would be used for?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: In connection with your giving the statement, was the name Vladimir Gojanovic mentioned?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: The name of Vladimir Gojanovic was mentioned because I had previously watched his testimony over the Internet.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: When you say you watched his testimony over the Internet, do you recall when that was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Was it before you gave your statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And the date that you gave your statement was May 8th, 2008; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: And it's your testimony that you watched his testimony here at the ICTY before you gave your statement; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: I was following it. I don't remember when it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: So were you mistaken when you just testified that you watched it before you gave your statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: That's what I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE
utterances.text: Okay. MS. DE LANDRI: Mr. President, I have no further questions of this witness. Just one housekeeping matter. Can we have in the record the translation of that military record linked to the exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But I'll say something about this exhibit in a minute. MS. DE LANDRI: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But we'll have that done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rak, I have a few questions for you. You said Mr. Babacic contacted you. It was that your --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- statement was needed. Did you speak with him about the testimony of Mr. Gojanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: We spoke about our memories of the action during Operation Storm. And it wasn't easy to recall all the events, since a great many years have passed. He told me that Mr. Gojanovic had given a statement or his testimony, whether it was over the Internet or what, that he was a member of my unit and he asked whether I remembered him. And that's how my statement was produced, where I said that, to the best of my recollection, he was not part of the action or a member of my unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now could you tell us in more detail when did Mr. Babacic approach you? Was that the day on which you gave the statement, or the day before, or two days before; could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: Earlier on. That was several days earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And it was by telephone that you got in touch; or did he come to your place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it happened in Sibenik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But do you remember whether it was by telephone or whether you met in person?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: We met.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it at that occasion that you discussed the untruthfulness of Mr. Gojanovic's -- his reports about being a member of your unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did Mr. Babacic make any link between the need to have a statement and the, as you said -- or at least as -- the untruthfulness of Mr. Gojanovic -- well, please, please. Please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: We discussed it and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we speak at the same time, the interpreters and transcribers will not be able to put everything on the record. So did Mr. Babacic explain to you that your statement was needed in relation to this -- what he considered to be an untruthful testimony or statement by Mr. Gojanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, as you said, you discussed the untruthfulness of Mr. Gojanovic, if I understood you well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't -- I must interject. I don't believe that was said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just, then, check exactly on the record what was said. One second, I have to find it. Yes, you discussed, as you told us, you said that Mr. Babacic told you that Mr. Gojanovic had given a statement on his testimony whether, over the Internet, or what, and he was a member of my unit and he had asked you whether he remembered -- I take it, you remembered him. To the best of your recollection, he was not part of the action or a member of your unit. So did I understand you well, that Mr. Babacic told you that Mr. Gojanovic had said that he had been a member of your unit and asked you whether your recollection was the same? Is that what you discussed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: This is what the conversation was like. That he had given a statement with what he said; whereas, my statement was based solely on my memory of these events. It was not the result of anybody exerting any sort of pressure or influence over me. It was purely the result of my memories.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you told Mr. Babacic at that time that you had no recollection of Mr. Gojanovic being a member of your unit. Did you tell him at that time; or did you wait until you gave your statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: I told him at the time that I did not remember him from the period of Operation Storm as a member of my unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did Mr. Babacic tell you whether this would or would not be -- or would not be a specific subject your interview?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: He didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You earlier said that you followed the proceedings through Internet. I'm not quite sure whether you, at a later stage --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- withdrew that or whether you had personally seen Mr. Gojanovic's testimony before this Tribunal through the Internet.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: Yes, I watched him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did it upset you what he said?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: In view of the fact that, to the best of my recollection, what he said were lies, yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And when you say "lies," you would include that he had been a member of your unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: He was not a member of my unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But my question was whether that part of his testimony also upset you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did the testimony you watched through the Internet, was this in any way encouraging you to give a statement or ...

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: I felt the duty to tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because Mr. Gojanovic had not told the truth. Is that how I have to understand your explanation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rak, if I would tell you that Mr. Gojanovic testified before this Court well after you had given your statement, could you explain your answers, in light of this fact which seems to be not in dispute between the parties and for which there is substantial evidence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Rak, you explained to us how the statement of Mr. Gojanovic upset you and that it encouraged you to -- to give a statement and that you had seen his testimony before you gave that statement; whereas, in this courtroom --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. President, but the witness's answer to your question was that it encouraged him to tell the truth. "I felt the duty to tell the truth," not I felt a duty to give a statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I asked him whether it encouraged him to give a statement. The question was about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, but his answer is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's -- Let me keep it, then, short. Mr. Gojanovic testified in this court well after the day you have given your statement. Could you reconcile that with the answers you have given to the questions that were put to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I took it from your answers that you had already seen and heard the testimony of Mr. Gojanovic before you gave your statement. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: I don't understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's keep matters short. From your answers, I took it that you, first, followed, through the Internet, the testimony of Mr. Gojanovic; and that, after that, you gave your statement on the 8th of May. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: I gave the statement about Operation Storm in the course of -- of the operation chronologically on the 8th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that was not my question. My question was whether you gave your statement after you'd heard and seen the testimony of Mr. Gojanovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll check your previous answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's page 79, lines 21 to 23.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think there is more than just one, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: There's also a reference at page 83 about the encouragement of the testimony, which, I think, is what Your Honour was referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's not further discuss in the presence of the witness. Yes, Mr. Rak, we'll carefully read again your testimony. The issue was that I understood from your answers that you had seen the testimony of Mr. Gojanovic which did upset you, because you said he gave lies and that when I asked you that, that that encouraged you. And then you said: "It encouraged me to tell the truth." Do you mean to say that it encouraged you to tell the truth in your statement, when being interviewed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: When the interview was held with me, I only told the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And when you said it encouraged you to tell the truth, did you mean to say that it encouraged you to tell the truth, as you said you did, during the interview?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: Yes. I was telling the truth when the interview was held with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you were encouraged to do so because you had heard the lies of Mr. Gojanovic. Is that how I have to understand your -- Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I don't think the witness knows there's a question pending to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think -- You have not answered my last question. Would you please do so? Or if you want me to repeat it, then I'll do so. Mr. Rak?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: Can you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll repeat my question. You told me that you were telling the truth when the interview was held with you. And then I asked you -- and whether you were encouraged to do so because you had heard the lies of Mr. Gojanovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: My statement would have been truthful, just as it is now, regardless of Gojanovic's statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was not my question. You apparently are evading to answer my question.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll then put the question in a different way. You earlier said that the false statement of Mr. Gojanovic encouraged you to tell the truth. Where did you then tell the truth, having become aware of the lies of Mr. Gojanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: In relation to his statement that he was a member of my unit, I answered that. That's -- that's why I stated the truth in my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I've no further questions for you, Mr. Rak. Have the questions of the Bench triggered any need to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: May I just ask one question, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you may. Let me -- one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rak, I just want to make sure we're clear: Do you know or do you recall whether you gave your statement to the Gotovina Defence before or after Mr. Gojanovic testified here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RAK
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has no further questions. MS. DE LANDRI: Nothing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. De Landri, also no further questions for you. MS. DE LANDRI: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rak, I'd like to thank you for coming to the videolink room and for having answered the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the parties to know that the Chamber, although considering to re-call one of the other witnesses, the witness is not available on the premises anymore. For that reason, the Chamber refrains from doing so; at least for this moment. This concludes the videolink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I know we're running late, Mr. President, so should we tomorrow move in the remaining exhibits under 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We could do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's no problem with that. And I don't know whether you have tendered all the documents you have shown, Ms. De Landri. I'm not quite sure. It could be you have, but I'm not certain about it. MS. DE LANDRI: I don't think so, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll deal with that also at the earliest occasion, and I have already stolen 15 minutes from interpreters, transcribers, security, everyone, and, of course, the parties. Therefore, we will adjourn and we'll resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 10th of September, quarter past 2.00, Courtroom III.
